item.title: Navy Rear Adm. Huffman meets South Korean counterparts at Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Navy Rear Admiral Greg Huffman met with South Korean naval leaders aboard the ROKS Hansando during a visit to Pensacola, according to the Navy's official news service. The meeting underscores the ongoing military training partnership between the two allied nations. The visit highlights the importance of naval cooperation in the region and…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Navy Rear Admiral Greg Huffman met with South Korean naval leaders aboard the ROKS Hansando during a visit to Pensacola, according to the Navy's official news service. The meeting underscores the ongoing military training partnership between the two allied nations.

The visit highlights the importance of naval cooperation in the region and comes as the U.S. and South Korea continue to strengthen defense ties. Pensacola has long served as a hub for international military training and collaboration, hosting personnel from allied nations.

Details about the specific agenda and outcomes of the meeting were not immediately available, but such visits typically focus on training coordination, operational planning, and strengthening relationships between allied naval commands.

item.title: Baptist Health Care Ramping Up Nurse Recruitment for Hospital Expansion
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Baptist Health Care is launching an active recruitment drive for registered nurses across its hospitals, medical parks, and clinics, citing growing patient volumes and the organization's ongoing expansion efforts. The health system plans to add 40 acute care beds to its Baptist Hospital campus, which is driving the hiring push. The recruitment…
item.content:encoded:
Baptist Health Care is launching an active recruitment drive for registered nurses across its hospitals, medical parks, and clinics, citing growing patient volumes and the organization's ongoing expansion efforts. The health system plans to add 40 acute care beds to its Baptist Hospital campus, which is driving the hiring push.

The recruitment effort is open to experienced nurses, new graduates, and those seeking career advancement. "A great nursing career is more than a job," said Joyce Nichols, the organization's vice president and chief nursing officer. "It's about being part of a team where your contributions are valued and your work has meaning."

Baptist Health Care is hosting open interview sessions for new graduate registered nurses on Thursdays—Nov. 19, Dec. 3, 10, and 17—from 10 a.m. to noon at the Bear Family Foundation Health Center, 6th floor, 125 Baptist Way in Pensacola. A broader nursing hiring event is also scheduled for Thursday, Jan. 7, 2027, from 3 to 6 p.m. at the same location. Candidates interested in learning more or applying can visit ebaptisthealthcare.org/jobs.

item.title: Milton offices closed Wednesday for Veterans Day; ceremony planned at Veterans Memorial Plaza
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton will close all municipal offices Wednesday, November 11, to observe Veterans Day, with normal business operations resuming Thursday, November 12. Residential sanitation collection schedules will not be affected. The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation is hosting a Veterans Day Ceremony and wreath-laying at Veterans…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton will close all municipal offices Wednesday, November 11, to observe Veterans Day, with normal business operations resuming Thursday, November 12. Residential sanitation collection schedules will not be affected.

The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation is hosting a Veterans Day Ceremony and wreath-laying at Veterans Memorial Plaza (5191 Willing Street) starting at 11 a.m., with activities expected to wrap up by noon. The ceremony honors the service and sacrifice of the nation's veterans.

Following the ceremony, the community is invited to American Legion Post 78 (6025 Spikes Way in Milton) for a flag retirement ceremony, bonfire, and cookout. Grover's Restaurant is providing food, with service from Santa Rosa County 4-H Club members and volunteers. For more details, contact vetplaza@santarosa.fl.gov.

item.title: Gulf Breeze Will Do Awards $52K+ in Grants to 10 Community Projects
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gulf Breeze Will Do distributed more than $52,000 in grants to 10 community projects on Sunday, Nov. 8, after an anonymous member stepped forward with an extra contribution to fully fund every finalist. The organization had $46,500 available from membership contributions, but the 10 finalists requested more than $52,000 combined. When a member…
item.content:encoded:
Gulf Breeze Will Do distributed more than $52,000 in grants to 10 community projects on Sunday, Nov. 8, after an anonymous member stepped forward with an extra contribution to fully fund every finalist.

The organization had $46,500 available from membership contributions, but the 10 finalists requested more than $52,000 combined. When a member donated nearly $6,000 to close the gap, Gulf Breeze Will Do was able to award 100 percent of requested funding to all finalists. "This is exactly why Gulf Breeze Will Do exists," Leslie Perino, the organization's president, said in a statement. "To see our members come together to make a difference in our community is incredibly rewarding."

The grants span four categories: art, recreation and sports; education; hardship support services; and public safety. Recipients include Gulf Breeze Middle School Band (for a transport trailer), Gulf Breeze High School biology program (for reusable frog dissection models), Soundside High School's ESE Department (for a student business program), and Gulf Breeze Elementary School (for AED machines and a water fountain replacement). The Santa Rosa Education Foundation also received funding for its Take Stock In Children laptop program.

Gulf Breeze Will Do received 18 grant applications this year requesting over $112,000. Volunteer committees reviewed submissions and selected the 10 finalists, who presented projects at the annual meeting where members voted on funding awards.

item.title: Pensacola Debris Crews Will Work Through Veterans Day
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola’s hurricane debris collection will continue through the Veterans Day holiday as the city works toward completing its first pass through neighborhoods. The city said in a November 9 update that its debris contractor was in the fourth week of the first round of collection. That pass is expected to be…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola’s hurricane debris collection will continue through the Veterans Day holiday as the city works toward completing its first pass through neighborhoods.


The city said in a November 9 update that its debris contractor was in the fourth week of the first round of collection. That pass is expected to be complete in late November, with a second round beginning shortly afterward.


During the second pass, residents can expect to see smaller debris haulers working narrow streets, cul-de-sacs and interior areas off main roads, the city said.


More than 541,850 cubic yards of debris had been collected within city limits, according to the update. The figure had also appeared in an earlier city report.


Regular sanitation collection for City of Pensacola customers will remain on its normal schedule during Veterans Day week, even though City Hall and other administrative offices will be closed Wednesday.


The city anticipates normal bulk and yard waste collections will resume in late December or early January. The Perdido Landfill is not currently accepting vegetative and construction and demolition debris, according to the city.

item.title: Escambia School Foundation Awards More Than $100,000 in Classroom Grants
item.dc:creator: news6334

The Escambia County Public Schools Foundation awarded $100,012.75 through its Grants for Excellence program for the 2026–27 school year, according to NorthEscambia.com . The projects…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Nineteen projects across Escambia County public schools are receiving support through more than $100,000 in classroom grants.


The Escambia County Public Schools Foundation awarded $100,012.75 through its Grants for Excellence program for the 2026–27 school year, according to NorthEscambia.com.


The projects cover a range of subjects and age groups. At Pensacola High School, one grant supports a hands-on cybersecurity learning and competition space. At Tate High School, another supports robotics.


Other awards include funding for 3D-printing technology at Booker T. Washington High School and an outdoor pollinator habitat and environmental learning laboratory at Ferry Pass Elementary School.


Teachers, schools and departments across the district received the grants. WEAR reported that the program also received support through the Consortium of Florida Education Foundations and a state school district education foundation matching grant program.

item.title: Senator Moody Secures $2.5B in FEMA Funding for Florida Disaster Recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody announced Monday that she has secured more than $2.5 billion in FEMA disaster assistance funding for Florida communities, fulfilling recovery efforts that have been pending since 2017. The funds will support over 500 projects across the state, including repairs to schools, restoration of critical infrastructure, debris…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody announced Monday that she has secured more than $2.5 billion in FEMA disaster assistance funding for Florida communities, fulfilling recovery efforts that have been pending since 2017. The funds will support over 500 projects across the state, including repairs to schools, restoration of critical infrastructure, debris removal, and emergency response costs.

Moody, who has held her Senate seat for less than two years, said she prioritized the recovery funding immediately upon taking office. "These are funds that communities have been waiting on for years, and something I began working on for Floridians as soon as I was appointed to the Senate," she said in a statement.

The senator also championed the TRACK Act, a transparency measure now law that requires FEMA to maintain a public status tracker so disaster victims can monitor the progress of their claims. The move addresses longstanding frustrations with the opacity of federal disaster aid processing.

Moody has been actively engaged in recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias, which struck Florida earlier this month. She led a delegation of Florida congressional members urging the president to approve the state's Major Emergency Disaster Declaration to expedite additional aid.

item.title: Pensacola Man Among 12 Arrested in Daphne Police Operation
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: DAPHNE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pensacola man was among 12 men arrested Friday during a multi-agency enforcement operation led by Daphne Police along the Interstate 10 corridor in Baldwin County. According to information reported by NBC 15, all 12 men face charges of solicitation of prostitution. The Pensacola man was identified as Jordan…
item.content:encoded:
DAPHNE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pensacola man was among 12 men arrested Friday during a multi-agency enforcement operation led by Daphne Police along the Interstate 10 corridor in Baldwin County.


According to information reported by NBC 15, all 12 men face charges of solicitation of prostitution. The Pensacola man was identified as Jordan Phillips.


Daphne Police said the operation focused on demand for commercial sex that can contribute to human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Officers from Orange Beach, Gulf Shores and Spanish Fort were among those who participated, along with the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office and Homeland Security Investigations.


Police said the Little Tree Project, a nonprofit organization that assists victims, provided open-source intelligence and other operational support.


Some of those arrested face additional charges, according to police. The available report does not identify any trafficking charges arising from the operation or state that trafficking victims were identified during it.


Blue RAM Media separately reported that an undercover operation based in Daphne resulted in prostitution-related arrests and listed Phillips among those arrested.

item.title: Patronis Defends SS United States Reef Plan as Legal Challenge Continues
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Congressman Jimmy Patronis is defending the plan to sink the historic SS United States as an artificial reef off Northwest Florida, as a preservation group continues its legal challenge to the project. Okaloosa County has scheduled the 990-foot ocean liner’s sinking for Thursday, Nov. 12, weather permitting. The…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Congressman Jimmy Patronis is defending the plan to sink the historic SS United States as an artificial reef off Northwest Florida, as a preservation group continues its legal challenge to the project.


Okaloosa County has scheduled the 990-foot ocean liner’s sinking for Thursday, Nov. 12, weather permitting. The vessel was scheduled to be towed from Mobile, Alabama, to a site in the Gulf ahead of the operation.


A federal judge denied an emergency request to stop the tow and sinking, although the underlying lawsuit remains active. The SS United States Preservation Foundation has sought to block the project, raising concerns about the ship’s preservation and environmental review.

Speaking on Pensacola Morning News, Patronis said he viewed the artificial reef as a way for people to continue experiencing the ship.


“If this boat was not sunk in this way, it would be scrapped,” Patronis said. “So, I mean, this is what this becomes. It becomes an underwater museum.”


Visit Pensacola is planning a free watch party at Seville Quarter on Thursday. Its event listing says the gathering begins at 9 a.m., with deployment operations scheduled to start around 10 a.m.


The ship, which entered service in 1952 and set a transatlantic speed record, was retired from passenger service in 1969.

item.title: Troopers Investigate Fatal Bicycle Crash on Gulf Breeze Parkway
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MIDWAY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating a crash that killed a bicyclist Sunday night on Gulf Breeze Parkway in Santa Rosa County. WEAR reports the crash happened around 8:45 p.m. at the intersection of U.S. 98 and Portside Drive. Troopers said a woman was riding a bicycle north across the parkway when she was…
item.content:encoded:
MIDWAY, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating a crash that killed a bicyclist Sunday night on Gulf Breeze Parkway in Santa Rosa County.


WEAR reports the crash happened around 8:45 p.m. at the intersection of U.S. 98 and Portside Drive. Troopers said a woman was riding a bicycle north across the parkway when she was struck by a westbound sedan.


The woman was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the report. Her identity had not been released.


The sedan’s driver, a 19-year-old Gulf Breeze man, was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries, WEAR reported, citing FHP.


Santa Rosa County Chief Deputy Randy Tifft discussed the crash Monday on Pensacola Morning News. He said deputies initially responded before the Highway Patrol took over the traffic investigation.


“No, I don’t know any of those details at this point,” Tifft said when asked about the circumstances of the crash.


Troopers have not released a determination about what caused the collision. The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Santa Rosa Sheriff’s Office Braces for Budget Impact After Amendment 3 Approval
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Santa Rosa County’s Sheriff’s Office is preparing for budget discussions after voters approved a property tax amendment expected to reduce revenue for local governments. Chief Deputy Randy Tifft told NewsRadio 92.3 that preliminary estimates put the potential impact on the county’s law enforcement taxing district…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Santa Rosa County’s Sheriff’s Office is preparing for budget discussions after voters approved a property tax amendment expected to reduce revenue for local governments.


Chief Deputy Randy Tifft told NewsRadio 92.3 that preliminary estimates put the potential impact on the county’s law enforcement taxing district at approximately $7 million. He said the district helps pay for patrol and deputy salaries.


“We haven’t started any discussions with the county as far as where are we going to go, how much of resources they’re going to make up for our loss,” Tifft said.


The estimate follows the passage of Amendment 3, which increases Florida’s homestead exemption for non-school property taxes beginning with the 2027 tax roll.


Tifft said the Sheriff’s Office typically begins preparing its next budget in January or February. He said no decisions have been made about how to address the projected loss.


“We’re going to do everything we can to make sure that we continue the same level of public safety as we always have, but there will be some cuts, unfortunately,” he said.


During the interview, Tifft also discussed a hypothetical comparison to deputy positions. He said he did not think the office would reach that worst-case scenario. No specific staffing reduction has been announced.

item.title: Santa Rosa County rabies vaccine clinic set for Friday at PSC-Milton
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Pet owners should enter at the second entrance on Highway 90 Westbound and follow directional signs. Veterinarians from The Ark…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County is hosting a drive-through rabies vaccination clinic this Friday, November 13, from 4 to 6 p.m. at Pensacola State College's Milton Campus, located at 5988 Highway 90. Pet owners should enter at the second entrance on Highway 90 Westbound and follow directional signs.

Veterinarians from The Ark Animal Hospital will administer rabies vaccines for $10 per pet, with cash and checks as the only accepted payment methods. Valid driver's licenses are required for check payments. Each vaccinated pet will receive a certificate of vaccination and rabies tag. The clinic is expected to vaccinate between 200 and 300 dogs and cats during the two-hour window.

Rabies is a fatal but preventable disease, and keeping pets current on vaccinations is the most effective protection. Pet owners are asked to keep animals secured in vehicles, crates, or on leashes during the clinic. For more information about the drive-through clinic, call 850-564-2278. The health department also recommends supervising pets outdoors, avoiding contact with wild animals, and contacting Santa Rosa County Animal Services at 850-983-4680 if an animal bite occurs.
